messages:
ops-bot: Paging oncall — elevated 429 rate observed for tenant meridian-finance in dedicated pool dp-meridian-02. 429 spikes started ~06:47 UTC, error ratio rising to ~18% over 5m. -> Blocking alerts to #incidents.

alex: on it, grabbing dashboards and pool metrics. can someone confirm contract override window exists? tagging @account-exec

account-exec: confirmed we have a 2h emergency lift clause in the contract. customer on call, said they can approve immediate temporary relief.

maya: metrics show sustained qps increase and connection saturation on GPU nodes 3-5. Redis KV cache miss rate up 8x — looks like repeated cold prefixes.

ravi: logs show model runtime queue length spikes + request requeues. saturation triggers our 429 throttle path when pool qlen > 250.

alex: quick mitigation options: 1) emergency quota override to increase tenant qps cap; 2) pin requests to a fallback smaller model temporarily; 3) scale dp-meridian-02 (slow). Which do we want now?

kendall: scale will take ~10-12m for new nodes to attach and become healthy. emergency override + model fallback gives fastest user-visible relief.

maya: agree. suggest emergency override to 2x and switch routing policy to prefer dp-meridian-03 (warm spare) for new requests. also enable per-tenant prefix caching for top 10 prompts we saw.

alex: customer confirmed they want override + model fallback. proceeding with 30m emergency lift, will monitor. tagging SRE procedure: @sre-bot can you record the action and run the safety checks?

sre-bot: Action logged: emergency_quota_override by alex at 06:55 UTC. Safety checks: auth token present, billing hold false, rollback timer set.

alex: running admin API command to apply temporary override now:

```bash
# internal admin API - temporary quota lift
curl -X POST https://admin.redwood.internal/api/tenants/meridian-finance/overrides \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer REDACTED' \
  -d '{"qps_override": 2.0, "duration_minutes": 30, "reason": "customer emergency - sustained 429s"}'
```

alex: response 200 OK. override active. routing changed to prefer dp-meridian-03 for read traffic.

maya: confirming telemetry — 2m after override 429 rate dropping to ~3%. latency P95 improved from 1.8s -> 1.1s. KV cache warm-up in progress.

ravi: also started a controlled model fallback for non-critical routes: switching from gpt-large-v2 to gpt-medium-v3 for low-priority endpoints. script kicked off.

account-exec: customer says their frontend errors are clearing. they requested we extend if still unstable in 20m.

alex: noted. setting a 20m checkpoint to evaluate extension. if we extend, will document reason + duration and route billing exception to finance.

maya: small anomaly: one node in dp-meridian-03 reported OOM at 07:01 UTC and was cycled by autoscaler. replaced node healthy at 07:04 UTC. we lost ~1 replica briefly but routing mostly unaffected.

kendall: setting up canary to route 5% back to original pool to validate stability before rollback.

ravi: health checks green. steady state qps back to normal for the tenant. 429 rate ~1.1%.

alex: preparing handoff to night oncall. summary: Emergency 30m quota override applied at 06:55 UTC for meridian-finance (dp-meridian-02), routing pref changed to dp-meridian-03, model fallback for non-critical endpoints, one OOM node replaced, metrics stabilized.

alex: handoff checklist to next oncall @maya:
- override expires 07:25 UTC (auto rollback scheduled)
- watch 429 rate and P95 latency for next 40m
- escalate to infra-eng if node replacement flaps >2 times
- if customer asks for extension, confirm authorization from account-exec and create billing exception ticket FIN-824

maya: ack. I'll take next 45m watch. creating short-lived dashboard with alert at 3% 429 threshold.

account-exec: reached out to meridian contact to log formal approval for any extension; they've already given verbal ok for initial 30m.

alex: adding post-incident items to backlog:
- run root cause eval on cold prefix flood and recommend pre-warming or adaptive cache (owner: eng-runtime)
- consider per-tenant burst profiles for enterprise pools (owner: product)

maya: also adding a test case to our chaos suite to exercise prefix cache storm and validate throttling behavior (owner: eng-ml).

ops-bot: scheduled follow-up check at 07:25 UTC.

maya: override will roll back automatically at 07:25 UTC. leaving snippet of rollback command in this thread in case we need manual revert: 

```bash
curl -X POST https://admin.redwood.internal/api/tenants/meridian-finance/overrides/revoke \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer REDACTED'
```

alex: thanks all. nice quick coordination. putting postmortem note in #postmortems after 24h and assigning action owners.

maya: reaction :thumbsup:

ravi: reaction :white_check_mark:

kendall: handoff complete, marking incident as mitigated for now.

ops-bot: Incident note appended to ticket INC-2026-981.
